sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Forest Service argues the Trails Act only assigns overall trail administration to the Park Service. It claims the Act does not transfer ownership of the land beneath the path. Conservation groups argue the Act converts all traversed land into Park Service units. They contend the Park Service manages the trail as a distinct national park unit.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The Forest Service wants the Court to affirm that the Trails Act does not transfer land ownership to the Park Service.
The conservation groups want the Court to rule that the Trails Act converts all trail land into Park Service units.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The Forest Service argues the statute assigns only administrative duties to the Park Service without changing land ownership.
The conservation groups argue the statute treats the trail as a distinct unit of the National Park System.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether the Park Service controls the land beneath the Appalachian Trail. It defines the scope of federal land management authority. It clarifies the legal status of trails within the national park system.
